name: Prezi
summary: AI presentation maker for dynamic, non-linear decks that stand out from standard slides — turn ideas into polished, interactive presentations fast.
best_for: presenters who want motion and zooming-canvas storytelling that stands out from slide decks — especially for talks, pitches and teaching
skip_if: your team just needs standard slides fast — conventional deck tools are quicker to learn and easier to hand off
honest_knock: The pricing table puts PDF export and portable presentations at Plus, not Standard, and our free account's AI editor locked PDF, PowerPoint and SCORM downloads to Plus. The zooming format is polarising: some audiences find it engaging, others find it disorienting.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: Prezi has a free plan, Basic, and three paid individual plans: Standard €5 a month, Plus €15 and Premium €25, all billed annually. Read on 28 September 2026 on prezi.com/pricing (which redirects to prezi.com/gts/pricing), in euros from a Netherlands exit, with every section of the comparison table opened; the three paid plans sit on the Individual tab, and Basic has a tab of its own, where it is shown next to Plus. Every paid plan on the page requires annual billing: there is no monthly-billing switch and no monthly-billed price, and the page advertises a 14-day free trial. Basic lets you make up to 5 projects that anyone can see, with 500 Prezi AI credits, and has no PDF export or PowerPoint converter. The comparison table is where the gates actually are: Prezi AI is 500 credits on Standard, with no period given, and unlimited above it. Its presentation exports, Export to PDF and portable presentations, start at Plus, as do video download and downloading as files in the Videos and Infographics sections; Standard is ticked on none of them, nor on presentation recording, smart branding, presenter view, voice-over or live remote presenting. On the Individual tab, presentation analytics and priority technical support are Premium only, as are five infographic rows: SQL connectors, iFrame import integrations, callouts, page linking and custom map import. The table has no PowerPoint-export row, and Prezi's help-centre article on downloading a presentation as PowerPoint names no plan either; the PowerPoint converter the table ticks on all three paid tiers, including Standard, is an import tool, even though the Plus card advertises PowerPoint import as a Plus benefit. The Business tab lists Plus €15 a month, Premium €25 a month and Teams €39 a month per user, all billed annually, and a Students & Educators tab has its own EDU plans that need a valid school email address. When we signed up the same day, Prezi's plan screen offered Plus €15, Premium €25 and Teams €39 a month (billed annually) with a trial, and an option to continue with Basic, but not Standard: the same lineup as the Business tab.

sessions.what: On 28 September 2026 we gave Gamma, Beautiful.ai, Prezi and Canva the same brief for a ten-slide investor deck: eleven facts about a made-up bakery chain and the rule to add no other numbers. We checked every deck against 15 tests written down before the first one was generated. Prezi ran on a new Basic (free) account.
findings: Prezi's AI editor opened in a pop-up window and built ten slides plus its zooming overview in under four minutes, using 150 of the 500 starting credits.

It added no numbers of its own and drew both charts to scale, but it made up a company website (kettlecrumb.nl), gave the CEO a gender the brief did not, and described 2025's actual revenue as a projection.
Asked once to 'Change the ask to €450,000 for 12%', it updated the ask slide but left 'Our €400,000 investment' on the use-of-funds slide, so the deck contradicted itself.

On Basic, PDF, PowerPoint (labelled editable) and SCORM downloads in the AI editor were all locked to Plus, and the only sharing option is Public, which the Dutch interface describes as anyone being able to find and view the deck ('iedereen kan dit vinden en bekijken'), with the account holder's name on the page. To take our deck offline we had to move it to the bin.
sessions.not_tested: One run on one day on the Basic plan; Plus may behave differently. We did not judge design quality. We downloaded and opened no exported file, so we have not checked whether the PowerPoint labelled editable keeps its text editable. Also untested: the PDF and PowerPoint download buttons on the public room page, shown to us on Basic and to logged-out viewers behind a sign-in, and the dashboard's Download PPTX.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
